notes: Measured on the de-leaked forecast-features-v2 dataset with the CS-014c split (fit 2023-01-01..2023-06-02, score the reserved final-28-date holdout 2023-06-03..2023-06-30). Reproduces the CS-014c rolling-origin report exactly on every shared metric (n_scored, n_zero_actual, group_mape_median_pct, p70_hit_rate, interval_coverage, group counts), so this baseline is directly comparable to it. These are a FLOOR to defend, not a target that passes the F5 band: the open per-group MAPE gate is a metric mismatch for small-count demand (see docs/decisions/CS-014b-acceptance-metric.md).
limitations: One-step-ahead, not multi-day-ahead. `items_lag_1h` and `items_roll_7d_same_hour` are built over the whole source window, so a scored holdout row uses actual demand from strictly earlier holdout hours. That is the intended rolling-origin protocol, but it is NOT what a week-ahead deployment does, and only `low_history` was scoped away from the holdout. A change that leans harder on the lag columns can improve this floor while degrading real multi-day-ahead accuracy.
Single fold. The `low_history` cutoff is derived from this window's tail, so leakage is closed for the final 28-day fold only; an earlier rolling-origin fold would still see its own period.

Not the acceptance gate. The gate ratified on 2026-11-23 (docs/decisions/CS-014b-acceptance-metric.md) is volume-weighted WAPE plus calibration, enforced by agents/demand_forecast/backtest.py over the official rolling-origin holdout, and the CS-014c backtest passes it. This file is a separate anti-regression floor for the fixed-origin measurement, not a restatement of that gate.
